title: Amazing Apples

themePack.overview: Toddlers explore apples as real fruit—looking, touching, smelling, sorting colors, and (with allergy checks) tasting. The week mixes short science looks, large-motor apple hunts, market pretend play, and process art that does not repeat the same stamp craft every day. Teachers keep experiences repeatable and washable, celebrate crunchy vocabulary, and offer non-food alternatives whenever tasting is not appropriate.
themePack.materials:
Real red, green, and yellow apples (whole)
Prepared apple slices for supervised taste test (allergy-checked)
Plastic play apples and baskets
Apple picture / color cards
Magnifying glasses (plastic)
Washable red/green/yellow paint and smocks
Apple-shaped sponges OR cookie cutters (vary art tools across days)
Construction paper, crayons, glue sticks, dot markers
Play dough and apple-sized balls
Sensory bin filler alternative: crumpled paper “orchard leaves” with plastic apples (no water beads)
Bean bags and floor spots for relays
Toy market stand props
Chart paper for favorite-apple graph
Wipes, towels, and labeled allergy notes
themePack.family: At the store or fridge, invite your child to find a red, green, or yellow apple and describe how it feels. If allergies allow, taste a slice together and talk about sweet, crunchy, or juicy. No orchard trip required—window shopping the produce aisle still builds rich apple talk.
milestones: Language: Uses apple color and sensory words (red, crunch, stem, sweet) during play and tasting talk
SEL: Waits for a turn with apples/baskets and tries a new food experience with supportive coaching
Motor: Stamps/sponges, carries baskets, rolls, and sorts oversized apple props
Cognition: Sorts apples by color/size and notices simple tree-to-fruit ideas with picture support

songs.title: Apple Colors Chant
songs.lyrics:
Red apple, green apple, yellow too,
Pick one up—which color are you?
Shine and wash and count with me,
Apples for our friends to see.
songs.motions: Hold up matching color cards; pretend pick; rub-shine motion; tap count to three.
songs.teacherDirections: Use real or play apples as visual anchors. Invite each toddler to show a color rather than answer verbally if needed.
songs.whenToUse: Monday circle with the apple basket reveal; Apple Color Sort warm-up
songs.transitionPurpose: Focus attention on apple colors before investigation

songs.title: Crunch, Munch, Pause
songs.lyrics:
Crunch, crunch, listen close,
Munch, munch—politely most.
Taste or touch, we take our time,
Thank you, apples—you’re so fine!
songs.motions: Tap fists together for crunch; wipe mouth politely for munch; hands in lap on take our time; thank-you wave.
songs.teacherDirections: Sing before Apple Taste Test. Emphasize that touching/smelling is a full participate option. Never pressure tasting.
songs.whenToUse: Taste-test preview and mealtime apple talk
songs.transitionPurpose: Set calm tasting manners and inclusion norms

songs.title: Roll, Pick, Parade
songs.lyrics:
Roll like an apple, round we go,
Pick the apples high and low.
Basket full—we march and sing,
Harvest friends, hear us ring!
songs.motions: Seated rock/roll arms; reach high/low pick; pretend carry basket; march in place.
songs.teacherDirections: Bridge Roll Like an Apple and Apple Basket Relay. Keep rolls seated or crawling—no tumbling piles.
songs.whenToUse: Gross-motor apple days and Friday harvest celebration
songs.transitionPurpose: Move from floor play into cleanup or parade

books.title: Apple Farmer Annie
books.author: Monica Wellington
books.why: Bright orchard-to-market sequence helps toddlers connect apples to growing, sorting, and sharing food.
before: Where do you think Annie’s apples grow?
during: What is Annie doing with the apples on this page?
after: Would you like to pick, wash, or sell apples in pretend play?
books.substitute: Apple picture cards plus Apple Colors Chant if the book is unavailable.

books.title: Apples and Pumpkins
books.author: Anne Rockwell
books.why: Seasonal farm visit text supports fall apple talk with clear, toddler-friendly illustrations.
before: Have you seen an apple tree or pumpkin patch?
during: Can you find the apples in the picture?
after: What would you put in your harvest basket?
books.substitute: Outdoor apple hunt with plastic apples and basket counting.

books.title: How Do Apples Grow?
books.author: Betsy Maestro
books.why: Simple nonfiction explains blossom-to-fruit ideas that pair with Apple Life Cycle and seed discovery.
before: What do you think an apple needs to grow?
during: Point to the flower, the tiny apple, or the tree.
after: How can we take care of living growing things?
books.substitute: Three life-cycle picture cards (flower, tiny apple, ripe apple) for a mini sequence talk.

books.title: Ten Apples Up On Top!
books.author: Theo LeSieg
books.why: Playful counting and balancing humor enriches number talk; use selectively for short read-alouds.
during: How many apples are on top now?
after: Let’s count five play apples into a basket.
books.substitute: Optional enrichment title—fully use if time allows; otherwise keep counting with real props.

books.title: The Biggest Apple Ever
books.author: Steven Kroll
books.why: Friendship-and-size story supports big/small apple comparisons without requiring a full week slot.
before: What makes an apple look big?
during: Who is trying to find the biggest apple?
after: Can you find a big apple and a small apple in our basket?
books.substitute: Optional fifth title for family lending or quiet shelf; prioritize top three for circle.

printableIdeas.title: Apple Color Picture Card Pack

printableIdeas.title: Apple Life Cycle Sequence Cards
printableIdeas.purpose: Flower → small apple → ripe apple cards for Friday science talk and seed discovery support.

teacherTips: Use stamp painting on one day only; later art days switch to collage, dough, or sponge tools so the week does not repeat identical stamp crafts.
Process prints will differ—display variety proudly.
Check and document allergies before any tasting; offer touch/smell-only participation.
Serve fresh slices with clean tongs; no sharing bitten pieces.
Apple Taste Test.safetyEmphasis: Allergy protocol required; have non-food apple props ready as the equal alternative.

teacherTips: Allergy check first; offer smell/look roles for non-tasters.
Serve tiny pieces and sanitize trays between groups.
Whole apples for looking/touching/smelling; wash hands before and after.
Keep tasting separate from investigation trays.
Use photo/color cards for voting so non-tasters fully participate.
Teacher handles cutting; toddlers view seeds in a sealed jar or large magnifying tray.
Seeds are not loose snacks—supervise closely.
Open-ended collage/dough tree—avoid identical template products.

bannedSongTitles: If You're Happy and You Know It (Apple Version)
themePack.safetyNotes: Confirm allergies before any apple tasting and provide equal non-tasting roles. Wash produce and hands; keep cut pieces refrigerated per program food rules. Avoid water beads and small loose seeds as play fillers. Art uses washable paint with smocks; vary tools so stamp painting is not daily. Supervise baskets/relays for safe carrying. Include children who cannot eat apples through smell, touch, sort, and pretend market play.

notes: Fixed missing catalog authors: Monica Wellington; Anne Rockwell; Betsy Maestro; Theo LeSieg (Dr. Seuss Beginner Books); Steven Kroll. Top 3 books fully enriched; titles 4–5 optional enrichment. Original apple chants replace copyrighted-risk apple-version pop songs. Art guidance deliberately varies media to avoid identical apple-stamp crafts each day.
